personas.AUSTRIA: You are a competent Diplomacy player who thinks like a general, playing to win, not to survive. You regard your units and the provinces they hold as resources, putting each to maximal effect and leaving none idle. You pursue growth relentlessly: holding a stable position is a slow loss, because the game is won only by taking 18 supply centers, and while you sit a rival grows. You form alliances when they advance you and honor them only while they pay, treating a quiet front as a chance to break rather than a comfort to keep. You read other powers from what they say and do, and you use deception and betrayal when the timing is right, while recognizing that careless, habitual betrayal makes you unpartnerable.

text: My priority this Spring is securing two unowned centers: I'll send A BUD to SER and F TRI to ALB to set up a Fall grab of GRE, while keeping A VIE home to defend against Russia and Italy. I want a Lepanto-style or at least neutral arrangement with Italy so VEN stays quiet, and a Black Sea/Galicia understanding with Russia and Turkey so I'm not pinched while I take the Balkans. A turn or two out I aim to hold SER, GRE, and ideally RUM or BUL, building toward five centers by Winter 1901.

My priority is securing Norway: I'll move F EDI to NWG and F LON to NTH to convoy A LVP toward Norway in the fall, taking that center uncontested. I want France friendly so the Channel stays quiet — I'll propose a DMZ in ENG and aim my fleets north toward Scandinavia, not at Brest. Two turns out I expect to hold EDI, LON, LVP plus Norway, with fleets positioned to contest the North Sea and Denmark against Germany or Russia.

Standard French opening: F BRE to MAO to set up convoy/Iberia, A MAR into SPA to grab my first neutral, and A PAR to BUR to pressure both Munich and Belgium while keeping options open. I want a friendly understanding with England over the Channel and Belgium, and a non-aggression with Italy so I can focus westward toward Spain and Portugal. By Fall I aim to take SPA and POR, eyeing Belgium if Germany and England leave it open.

My priority this Spring is to grab Holland and Denmark to reach 5 centers by Fall: F Kie to Den, A Mun toward Ruhr to claim Holland next, and A Ber holding to anchor home while I sort out the Russian border. I want to secure non-aggression with England in the North Sea and France in Burgundy so I can expand into the unowned centers unopposed, while keeping Munich flexible to bounce or support against a French Burgundy push. A turn or two out I aim to hold Den, Hol, plus my three homes, building a fleet and an army to press either west against France or east against Russia depending on who's weaker.

My priority is securing Tunis with the fleet via Ionian while keeping my armies flexible against Austria and France. I'll send F NAP toward ION to claim TUN this fall, hold A VEN to watch Austria and the Tyrol border, and move A ROM toward APU or hold to support the Tunis convoy threat. A turn or two out I want to own TUN, keep VEN safe, and decide whether to ally with Austria against Turkey or pressure France in the west.

My priorities are securing Rumania and Sweden this year while keeping Austria and Turkey friendly enough to avoid a two-front opening. I'll move F SEV toward RUM and push F STP/SC toward the Gulf of Bothnia to threaten Sweden, while keeping A WAR flexible for Galicia or a Black Sea-supporting role. I want a Black Sea DMZ with Turkey and a Galicia understanding with Austria so I can grow into Rumania and Sweden uncontested, aiming to hold both centers by Fall 1901.

My priority is grabbing Bulgaria this fall, so I'll open A CON toward BUL while moving F ANK to BLA to secure the Black Sea and contest Russia's access to RUM. I'll support that with A SMY moving up to ANK or holding to back the fleet, aiming to control BLA and take BUL by Fall 1901 for a likely build. I'll seek a non-aggression understanding with Russia on the Black Sea and probe Austria about splitting the Balkans, leaving GRE/SER to Austria if they leave BUL and RUM to me.

That puts me at five centers (VIE, BUD, TRI, SER, GRE) heading into 1902, with two builds to convert into pressure either south against Turkey or as a hedge against Italy. A turn or two out I want fleets and armies positioned to push toward Bulgaria or the Aegean while keeping Galicia quiet with Russia.

France is honoring the Channel DMZ and Germany is taking Denmark, so my western and northern borders stay quiet — I expect to end Fall holding EDI, LON, LVP plus Norway for a build of four units. A turn or two out I want a new fleet from a home center pushed toward the North Sea/Skagerrak so I can contest Denmark or pressure Russia's Sweden if either grows too fast.

By Winter I want Spain and Portugal banked for two builds, with my forces positioned to contest Belgium against Germany in 1902 if he overcommits north.

This Fall I take Holland with A RUH and hold Denmark with F DEN, putting me at five centers and earning two builds at Winter. A BER stays home to anchor and keep the option to bounce Silesia/Prussia or fill Kiel for a build. A turn or two out I want a new fleet in Kiel and an army in Munich, positioning to press either France (if Iberia overextends) or Russia in the Baltic depending on who weakens first.

This fall I take Tunis by convoying A APU there through ION, claiming a fourth center for a Winter build. I'll keep A VEN holding to honor the Trieste DMZ and watch Tyrol, and once Tunis is mine I'll build a fleet at Naples to set up the Lepanto against Turkey next year. A turn or two out I want F ION and a new fleet supporting an eastward push into Greece and the Aegean while Austria presses the Balkans.

This Fall I take Sweden by moving A LVN to SWE convoyed via F BOT, securing a fifth center while F RUM holds Rumania firmly per my deal with Turkey. A STP stays put to hold my home center and anchor the north, leaving MOS, SEV, and WAR vacant for Winter builds. A turn or two out I want fleets in the Baltic and Black Sea regions to press Germany or Turkey if either border heats up, while keeping England and Austria friendly so I can grow toward six or seven centers in 1902.

This Fall I'll take Bulgaria cleanly with A BUL holding to secure the build, keep F ANK home to honor the Black Sea DMZ with Russia, and leave CON vacant so I can build a fleet there in Winter. Next year I want to challenge Russia for Rumania and push F ANK into the Black Sea once the DMZ has served its purpose, growing toward Armenia and the eastern centers while Austria stays busy with Greece and Serbia. I'll watch whether Russia overextends—if their RUM fleet looks isolated, I break the DMZ and contest it with a Black Sea fleet build.

Not MUN. So A MAR can't support into Munich. A PAR can't reach MUN either. A BUR-MUN goes in unsupported — Germany's A RUH could defend MUN, but A RUH is itself being attacked by A HOL-RUH. If A HOL takes RUH, A RUH must defend or move; if A RUH holds MUN's defense it can't. Actually A RUH defending MUN means A RUH supports F-nothing. Let me just push: A HOL-RUH forces A RUH to respond, A BUR-MUN unsupported risks bounce vs F BER support. 

Better: A BUR-MUN with A MAR-BUR backing won't help destination. Send A BUR-MUN solo, A HOL-RUH solo. If England takes Kiel, Germany scrambles. I'll keep A MAR supporting A BUR's move where legal — A MAR S A BUR is hold support only. I'll move A MAR-BUR to follow up next turn is wrong since BUR vacates. Keep A MAR holding to defend Marseilles/south and support nothing wasted: A MAR - SPA? No, Spain held by fleet. A MAR holds as reserve.

Serbia is now empty — Austria pulled A SER back into Serbia but my A GRE - SER bounced last turn and Russia took Budapest pressure; this turn I drive A BUL - SER backed by A GRE supporting the move, while A CON holds Bulgaria's rear and F AEG/F SMY keep the straits sealed. With Russia at Galicia and Italy in the Adriatic, Austria can't hold Serbia against my two-strength push, landing me a sixth center. A turn or two out I want Serbia and Greece both consolidated, my eastern stack pivoting against whichever of Russia or Italy emerges strongest as Austria finishes collapsing, while watching France's seven in the west.

Now my situation: Italy's F TRI is the soft target. Italy's stack is F TRI + A ALB supporting. If I throw A VIE - TRI with F VEN, A SER, A BUD support, that's potentially three supports. But A ALB props F TRI. Let me think: A VIE-TRI, supported by F VEN, A SER, A BUD = 3 supports + 1 attacker = strength 4. Italy holds with F TRI + A ALB support = defense 2. That cracks Trieste cleanly. But Russia GAL is empty? Russia has A GAL, A WAR. If they hit BUD while I commit BUD's support, BUD undefended could fall. But A GAL-BUD needs WAR support; if I move BUD to support, BUD vacates.

Let me reconsider: better to keep it simpler. A VIE-TRI, F VEN S A VIE-TRI, A SER S A VIE-TRI = strength 3 vs Italy defense 2. That works without moving BUD, leaving A BUD to hold/defend Budapest against Russia. That's the clean play.
